studies.label: Dutch EQ-5D-5L heteroskedasticity and heterogeneity valuation study
studies.family_rationale: The principal contribution is an evaluation of how controlling heteroskedasticity, taste heterogeneity, and scale heterogeneity affects EQ-5D-5L valuation. The pits-scale value set is an important output, but it is produced as part of the methodological case analysis.

items.statement: The authors interpreted the small number of significant coefficient differences and the value correlations as evidence that PC and BWS case 2 might be used interchangeably.

items.statement: The authors concluded that simultaneous control of heteroskedasticity, taste heterogeneity, and scale heterogeneity improved valuation by reducing the influence of the garbage class and respondents who failed the dominance task.

items.statement: The authors considered the resulting pits-scale Dutch EQ-5D-5L value set moderately concordant with the original values and recommended testing the method in larger studies with richer behavioral information.
